set.name: La Finette, Taverne d'Arbois
set.hook: Arbois's log-table tavern since 1961: Comté fondue, poulet au Vin Jaune, an all-Jura wine list.
set.why: La Finette has fed Arbois since 1961 from a timber-built room off avenue Pasteur: varnished log tables set round barrels, folk décor on every wall and a vaulted cellar below. The food is the Jura farmhouse canon served in quantity, from a pot of Comté fondue kept bubbling at the table to chicken deglazed with Vin Jaune and morels, Morteau sausage and Jura trout. The wine list stays inside the department, so it doubles as a first lesson in Savagnin and Trousseau.
set.verdict: Go for the room and the classics, not for finesse. Gault&Millau 2026 gives it 11/20 and says the technique does not always convince, probably because of the crowds, while praising the terrace, the mood and generous plates. Diners rate it highly on Google (4.6 from about 2,700 reviews). Order the fondue or the Vin Jaune chicken and drink a local bottle.
set.signature: Poulet (volaille) au Vin Jaune et morilles
set.caveat: In Arbois, about 40 km north of Lons by road; busy at weekends and in season, so book; hours vary by source, call ahead

set.name: Le Caveau des Jacobins (Poligny)
set.hook: The Arbois co-op's tasting cellar inside the former Jacobin church of Poligny: all the Jura wines in one stop.
set.why: The cellar is in Poligny, not Lons. Its wines come from the Fruitière Vinicole d'Arbois, the growers' cooperative that took over the Poligny co-op, and the tasting room fills the former church of a Dominican convent. Since the friars left, the building has served as a gunpowder works under Napoleon, a grain hall and a cooperative wine cellar; the Fruitière moved in in 2005. One counter pours Poulsard, Trousseau, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Savagnin, plus Crémant, Macvin, Vin de Paille and Vin Jaune.
set.verdict: Useful on the road between Lons and Arbois if you want the whole Jura range in one free tasting before driving out to the domaines. It is a cooperative shop, not a caviste with growers' bottles, so do not expect Macle or Tissot here. Opening hours and a possible renovation closure need a phone call first.
set.signature: A side-by-side of Savagnin ouillé, Savagnin sous voile and Vin Jaune
set.caveat: In Poligny, about 30 km north of Lons, not in central Lons; hours conflict and an older note mentioned renovation, so phone first

set.hook: The Jura's biggest weekly market: Thursday food on Place de Verdun, a Saturday organic market on Cours Sully.
set.why: On Thursday Lons fills two squares: a morning food market on Place de Verdun and a day of clothes and hardware on Place du 11 Novembre, from about 7 until 5. Saturday morning is smaller and food only, organic and short-chain stalls on Cours Sully. Late October is when Mont d'Or comes back in its spruce box, beside Comté of several ages, Morteau sausages with their wooden plug, jars of cancoillotte and fir honey.
set.verdict: Thursday morning is the one to plan around: the food stalls are on Place de Verdun and thin out by midday. Saturday is the quieter, greener version. The new mayor, elected in March 2026, has tested moving the Thursday market to Place de la Liberté and rue du Commerce, so check the squares before you go.

set.name: Fromageries Vagne (Épicuréa, Poligny)
set.hook: The Vagne family's affineur shop in Poligny, Comté capital: wheels from 10 to 24 months, Jura wines alongside.
set.why: No Vagne shop exists on rue du Commerce in Lons. The Vagne fromageries are real, though, and sit up the road: the family house, founded in 1926 according to a 2023 review, sells from Épicuréa on Place des Déportés in Poligny, with Comté aged from 10 to 24 months, regional wines and charcuterie. Its ripening cellars are on the edge of Poligny, and in Château-Chalon a former village fruitière has become a Vagne shop and small museum.
set.verdict: Worth it if you are already driving the Poligny-Arbois road and want Comté from an affineur rather than a supermarket counter. It is not a Lons address: for cheese inside town, use the Thursday market or a rue du Commerce fromager. Hours are split and need checking; nothing dated 2026 was found.

set.name: Chocolaterie Pelen
set.hook: Lons's family chocolatier since 1899, roasting its own beans, with a tea room upstairs.
set.why: Joseph Pelen opened as confectioner and chocolatier in 1899, and the house kept the Prince d'Orange name he took in 1902. The boutique on rue Saint-Désiré is Belle Époque and runs over two floors, with a tea room upstairs. Pelen is one of very few French chocolatiers to roast its own cocoa beans, and Arnaud Pelen, of the family, makes the praliné. Regulars come back for the écureuil, the squirrel-shaped house speciality.
set.verdict: The chocolate shop Lons is known for, and the place for an edible gift to carry back aboard. Gault&Millau lists it as an artisan. Recent reviews are mixed: praise for the pastries and the écureuil, complaints about prices, early closing and a cool welcome, with a newer note that the tea room has improved. Buy the chocolate; do not count on a late coffee.
set.signature: The écureuil, and the Galet de Chalain praliné-nougatine
set.caveat: The shop is 1 rue Saint-Désiré in the centre; rue Blaise Pascal is the industrial-zone site. Tea room closes early

wine.title: Fondue, buffet, co-op counter
wine.story: Jura wine is mostly drunk where it is made, so the wine tables sit on the slope north of Lons rather than in town. In Arbois, La Finette has served Comté fondue and Vin Jaune chicken at varnished log tables since 1961, and pours only Jura bottles. Across town on Place Faramand, the Bistrot des Claquets runs as a bar from morning to about nine at night and sends out one lunch dish a day with a cold buffet, the wine chosen from a shelf of local natural growers. In Poligny, the Caveau des Jacobins pours the Fruitière Vinicole d'Arbois range, from Poulsard to Vin Jaune, inside the former church of a Dominican convent.
wine.where: La Finette, Arbois; Le Bistrot des Claquets, Arbois; Caveau des Jacobins, Poligny

street.title: Thursday squares, Comté cellars
street.story: The Jura pantry is bought rather than eaten out, and most of it is cheese. In Lons the Thursday market, the largest in the department, runs from about seven to five across two squares, with food stalls on Place de Verdun in the morning; a smaller organic market fills Cours Sully on Saturday mornings. Thirty kilometres north, the Vagne family, affineurs since 1926, sell Comté aged ten to twenty-four months from their Poligny shop on Place des Déportés. Back in the centre of Lons, Chocolaterie Pelen has made chocolate since 1899, roasting its own beans, in a two-floor boutique on rue Saint-Désiré with a tea room upstairs.
street.where: Marché de Lons-le-Saunier, Place de Verdun; Fromageries Vagne, Poligny; Chocolaterie Pelen, Rue Saint-Désiré
